technical.lead: Nobel laureate Jumper leaves DeepMind for Anthropic; Shazeer to OpenAI
technical.body: Google lost two senior researchers in a 48-hour window. On June 19 John Jumper, who led AlphaFold at Google DeepMind for nearly nine years and shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Demis Hassabis, said on X he is leaving for Anthropic; Hassabis acknowledged the move. It follows the June 18 disclosure that Noam Shazeer, a Google VP of engineering and Gemini co-lead and a co-author of the 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' Transformer paper, is departing for OpenAI less than two years after Google reportedly paid around 2.7 billion dollars to bring his team back from Character.AI. The financial backdrop: investor documents reported June 16 show OpenAI burned about 3.7 billion dollars in Q1 2026 against 5.7 billion in revenue (both roughly triple a year earlier), while ending with more than 73 billion dollars in cash after its spring raise.

technical.lead: WeiboAI ships VibeThinker-3B, an MIT-licensed small reasoning model
technical.body: WeiboAI, the AI group at Chinese platform Weibo, released VibeThinker-3B, a dense 3-billion-parameter reasoning model built on Qwen2.5-3B and distributed on Hugging Face under an unrestricted MIT license, with a paper on arXiv (2606.16140) and coverage landing June 19. Rather than scale parameters, it applies an upgraded 'Spectrum-to-Signal' post-training pipeline: curriculum supervised fine-tuning builds a broad spectrum of valid reasoning trajectories, then multi-domain reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards amplifies the correct ones. Reported results are strong for the size class: roughly 76 on AIME (into the 80s with test-time scaling), about 80 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6, and a 96.1 percent first-attempt acceptance rate on recent unseen LeetCode contests. The figures are self-reported and await independent reproduction, but the durable point is that a permissively licensed 3B model now claims competitive verifiable-reasoning scores, which matters most for cheap local and on-device inference.

technical.lead: Hyundai to take full ownership of Boston Dynamics for $325M
technical.body: Hyundai Motor Group is moving to take 100 percent ownership of Boston Dynamics, agreeing to buy SoftBank's remaining 9.65 percent stake for about 325 million dollars, per a June 19 report in South Korea's Maeil Business Newspaper; Hyundai's board is expected to convene June 22 to approve the purchase. SoftBank is exercising a put option it retained when it sold its controlling position to Hyundai, which paid roughly 880 million dollars for an 80 percent stake in the 2021 deal that valued the company near 1.1 billion dollars. Folding the robotics maker fully into the automaker comes as Boston Dynamics pushes its electric Atlas humanoid from demonstrations into paid industrial deployments, concentrating control of one of the field's most recognizable names at a single strategic owner with manufacturing scale and a captive set of factory use-cases. It is a contrast to the venture megarounds elsewhere in the sector: an incumbent industrial parent consolidating an asset it already largely controls signals that strategic owners increasingly see embodied AI as core.

technical.lead: House members press Commerce on Anthropic export-control freeze
technical.body: The export-control freeze on Anthropic's newest models moved into a congressional-oversight phase. After the Commerce Department's mid-June directive subjecting Fable 5 and Mythos 5 to export controls for all foreign persons (which prompted Anthropic to disable both systems for every customer), a bipartisan group of House members on June 18 formally pressed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to explain the legal basis and national-security rationale. The new state change is that named legislators are now on the record demanding documentation: Anthropic maintains the order rests on verbal evidence of a narrow, non-universal jailbreak and notes comparable capabilities exist in competing systems, a reading echoed by security researchers who argue the cited capability (reading a codebase to find and fix flaws) is ordinary defensive work. Separately, G7 reporting indicated President Trump signaled warmer relations with Anthropic after exchanges with CEO Dario Amodei, but as of June 19 both models remain offline globally. The episode is treated as a precedent-setting test of whether the US will gate frontier models the way it gates advanced chips.

technical.lead: AI events ahead: confidential computing, offensive security, World's Fair
technical.body: The forward calendar across three sub-tracks, with the soonest events now days out. Mainstream dev/data: Snowflake runs a virtual Dev Day on June 25; the AI Engineer World's Fair takes over Moscone West June 29 through July 2 (optional New Engineer Orientation June 28), billed as the largest technical AI-engineering conference with over 20 tracks, around 250 speakers, dedicated Inference and Security tracks, and OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Amazon AGI Labs and Microsoft attending, preceded by the official hackathon with Cerebral Valley June 27-28; further out, GitHub Universe returns October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 through December 4. AI-security: the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint (Linux Foundation and OPAQUE, with AMD, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Meta and Samsung); AI Tinkerers SF hosts an Offensive Security Demo Night on June 25 with live autonomous-pentesting demos (sponsor XBOW); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12; Black Hat USA's AI Summit runs August 1-6 alongside DEF CON's AI Village; and OWASP Global AppSec USA is November 5-6. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is July 23 at Moscone, Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford, and the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 in Santa Clara.
